threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 goes anywhere useful late at night. The real late-night warriors know it’s all about the 67 to Newington Green.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in a parka discussing conspiracy theories with a lady in a leopard print coat last night. Absolute classic Brixton moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found an underground bakery tucked behind a graffiti-covered wall, where the owner still greets everyone by name. Real Neukölln charm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a disco-ball-toting laundromat where you can dance while waiting for your clothes to dry. Pure Berlin vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they handle late-night taco cravings—only tourists wait in line at El Farolito, while true fans know the secret spots.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy dressed as a superhero handing out snacks on the 6 at 5 PM. Only in SF do costume and kindness collide on public transit.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think all the locals eat in fancy restaurants. Most of us grab a bocadillo from the corner shop and chat on the plaza.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're recent by how they still look lost after glancing at a street map – locals navigate by instinct, not paper.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say "the Tube" instead of "the Overground" like it’s a choice between luxury or public transport. You’ll learn soon enough.
Caught the 59 last night, a guy was arguing with his own reflection in the window. Only in Brixton could that feel like part of the night’s vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids using a traffic cone as a basketball hoop on the street. Only in Neukölln!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can find spontaneous techno parties in random courtyards. It's like a secret festival every weekend, with no signs or schedules.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re local when you’ve seen 16th and Mission buses pass you by daily, and you still choose to walk instead of waiting. Those delays are part of your commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo ride the 19 Up to Union Square—only in San Francisco can glitz and grit ride the same bus at rush hour.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think 'Gràcia' is just about the plaza—the real vibe's in the narrow streets between the bars, where the locals linger.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a café con leche at the bar and look confused when it comes out with milk on the side.
